newsitem.title: BELGIUM: British Midland to order at least 20 aircraft.
newsitem.headline: British Midland to order at least 20 aircraft.

text.p: British Midland plans to order at least 20 new aircraft in the next few weeks, chairman Sir Michael Bishop told a news conference on Thursday.

"We expect in the next few weeks to be announcing a significant order for new aircraft," Bishop said, adding that the company was "in the final a stages of evaluation" for an order of "not less than 20" aircraft.
He said the aircraft under consideration were Boeing's 757 and 737-800 models and the Airbus 321.
"We want to replace some of our earlier stage three aircraft," he said.

Bishop added that constraints on slots at various European airports meant that within a couple of years the company's 150-seater aircraft would not be big enough and that it would have to move into the 200-seater range.

Bishop was in Brussels to comment on the April 1 start-date for liberalisation of the EU's civil aviation market, from when EU airlines will have "cabotage" rights to fly domestic services point-to-point in any of the bloc's 15 countries.
"We think that April the first will be something of an anti-climax. We do not think there is going to be a rash of new start-up airlines," he said.

"I do not think that there is great appetite in the airline industry to rush into a lot of cabotage," he said, citing the mixed success of British Airways's efforts to do just that using TAT in France and Deutsche BA in Germany.

"We have no plans to do that at the moment. We would regard British Airways as a very formidable competitor and an efficient airline and we have noticed the experience they have had with these services."
"I think that for a company of our size, it would be unwise at our stage of development to expose ourselves to these kinds of costs," he said.
